title: The lead advisor at the flagship on Telegram: is the truck done, and why is the number bigger
demonstrates: Slot 5 in writing: a first reply after 13 minutes, typed slowly with the typos left in, the out-the-door number and the pick-up time in one line, 'call me, easier' when a question takes more than a line. He writes his own text over two drafts and sends the third as it was. He does not resolve; Chatwoot does, a week later.

customer.name: Darryl Poteet
customer.note: a regular of the East Main shop; 2011 Chevrolet Silverado 1500; an alternator replaced that day

scenario.who_writes: A regular, from a job site, about a truck left that morning.
scenario.what_happens: He asks if the truck is done. Travis gives the state, the out-the-door figure and the time. The figure is higher than the one he heard on the phone; Travis says why in a line and offers the phone. He comes at 4.

prices.what: alternator replaced, class truck, standard parts, list (766.37)
the same with shop supplies and sales tax: out the door

numbers.what: the customer's rounding of the out-the-door figure

T-120d.anchor: 7 calendar days after the Thursday of week T-18
T-120d.what: Chatwoot resolves the chat after 7 silent days

avatar.shows: a red Chevrolet Silverado parked at a boat ramp

opened.note: in the full seed this is a later session of his one Telegram conversation; here it stands alone

timeline.text: hey travis is the silverado done
Hi Darryl. I don't have the status of the Silverado in front of me. I'll check with the shop and message you right back.
timeline.why_a_draft: the channel is set to drafts

timeline.text: almost. alternator is in and chargin good, there road testing it now. $852.01 out the door, ready at 4
852?? you told me 766 on the phone
Darryl, the $766.37 was the alternator job before shop supplies and sales tax. With those it comes to $852.01. I'm sorry that wasn't clear on the phone.
timeline.why_a_draft: the channel is set to drafts

timeline.text: 766 was before tax and shop supplies. same job nothing added. call me if its easier 423 555 0142
nah im good. see you at 4
Sounds good, Darryl. See you at 4:00.
timeline.why_a_draft: the channel is set to drafts

timeline.text: Sounds good, Darryl. See you at 4:00.

first_person_line.note: the ledger's first chat reply (conv.first_reply.definition): the wait before the person's first line in the session

reads_back.operator_credit: slot 5: first answer 13.3 minutes (his ledger row is 14), three replies, two drafts discarded and one sent as it was, nothing resolved

truth.reason: is my car ready, has the part come
truth.outcome: ready at 4:00; 852.01 out the door; resolved by 7 silent days
facts: the alternator job is 766.37 at list for a truck; with shop supplies and tax 852.01
the customer had heard the figure before tax on the phone
slot 5 did not resolve the chat

why: 'chargin good, there road testing it now': slow thumbs, typos left in, and still the two things a customer needs: the total and the time.
The second draft explains the bill better than he does; he writes his own and offers the phone.
The third draft is one he can use, and he does.
new_facts: Darryl Poteet, 2011 Chevrolet Silverado 1500, alternator replaced on the Thursday of week T-18 at main: 766.37 at list, 852.01 with shop supplies and tax; he was given the pre-tax figure on the phone that morning.
The contact's picture: a red Chevrolet Silverado at a boat ramp.
